thread:
elaine (SRE): heads-up — we just started getting a bunch of escalations (429s) from several customers around 14:02 UTC. spike correlates with a deploy of limiter-config v2.1. @omar can you pick this up?
omar (oncall): on it. seeing 5xxs? or strictly 429?
elaine (SRE): mostly 429s with intermittent 502s from the proxy when the limiter suddenly rejected large concurrent request bursts. stack traces attached in logs: `limiter: token_refill() overflow at bucket_id=global, rate=200/s, burst=1000`
maria (support): Customer C reported production break, giving us request ids: req-67a9, req-67ad, req-67b0. They say it started at 14:02 and affected background ingestion jobs and API calls. I'll open escalation tickets.
omar (oncall): I can see the same in metrics. global-limiter token_count went negative briefly and then clipped which caused the proxy to short-circuit. looks like the refill math used millis instead of seconds after the config change.
jake (infra): which config change? I rolled forward the limiter config from staging -> prod at 13:58. it updated burst to 1000 to allow bursts for Dedicated customers.
sophie (eng-runtime): oh hmm. the new config uses `refill_interval_ms` param we added for micro-batching; if the code expects seconds we double-count. will check code path.
deploy-bot: deployment jake/limiter-config v2.1 promoted to production at 13:58 UTC by jake. CI: passed.
elaine (SRE): mitigation: for now I've applied a temporary rule to cap global burst to 200 at the proxy layer and enabled 429-smoothing so we don't short-circuit proxies. rolling that now (ETA 2m).
omar (oncall): confirmed, 2m after applying cap we see 429 rate drop and successful retry rates improve. latency back to baseline for most routes.
maria (support): updating customers. CS ticket numbers: CS-4621 (Cust C), CS-4622 (Cust D), CS-4623 (Cust E). telling them we rolled a mitigation and a rollback is planned.
jake (infra): I can roll back limiter-config to v2.0 now if that's preferred. can do a quick canary then full rollback.
sophie (eng-runtime): prefer rollback to v2.0 — the new param parsing bug needs a fix. do we have an easy feature-flag to gate this?
jake (infra): not for config promoted via infra tool; rollback will fully revert. starting canary now on 2/10 nodes.
deploy-bot: rollback job initiated by jake at 14:11 UTC. canary on nodes 4/5.
omar (oncall): monitoring — token refills look stable, 429s continuing to decline.
elaine (SRE): good. once rollback finishes can we run a small load test reproducer (burst pattern) from staging with the v2.1 parser fix to validate? also need unit test for millis vs seconds case.
sophie (eng-runtime): yes — i'll add a unit + integration test. quick patch: change `parse_refill_interval` to accept both ms and s with suffixes (e.g., "500ms", "2s") and add validation. pushing PR to fix and adding test vectors.
jake (infra): rollback complete at 14:18 UTC. full cluster now on v2.0. metrics look normal.
omar (oncall): final check — 429s essentially resolved, a couple of remaining customer retries in flight. marking incident as mitigated.
maria (support): I'll confirm with customers and close CS tickets once they ack. sending templated note: "We experienced brief rate-limiting caused by a configuration parsing bug in a recent deploy. We rolled back and applied temporary caps. Engineers are adding tests and will re-roll with fixes. Apologies for disruption"
elaine (SRE): notes for post-incident: 1) don't allow silent units change in config (ms vs s) — enforce units; 2) add canary window longer (10m) for limiter changes; 3) add per-customer throttles to avoid global bucket blowups; 4) expose more granular limiter metrics (per-bucket refill delta). I'll write the postmortem.
sophie (eng-runtime): I'll open PR with fix and tests (PR#8123). will also add parsing validation + lint rule for config schema.
jake (infra): propose adding feature-flag gating for limiter config promotions — infra can implement default OFF for big changes. filing infra ticket INFRA-708.
omar (oncall): also recommend adding an automated smoke test that does a 5000 req burst against canary nodes and checks that limiter doesn't permit > configured burst.
elaine (SRE): agreed. action items: [elaine] postmortem draft, [sophie] PR & tests, [jake] infra ticket + rollout gating, [omar] add smoke test to canary harness, [maria] customer follow-ups.
maria (support): noted. I'll ping customers when stable and track acknowledgements.
elaine (SRE): closing thread for now — will post postmortem link here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
